LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION (THE COMMA)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma), part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: which the comma is used and then write down some sentences on a digital device. Why do you think we use a comma when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise the use of a comma correctly in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use the comma correctly in listing items,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. adopt the use of the comma in writing. ● Individually, learner is guided to identify commas from writings on wall charts/ chalk board/digital and print resources. ● Individually, learner is guided to use the comma correctly in written exercises, with peers. ● In pairs, learners are guided to use commas to write lists of items/ names. ● In pairs, learners are guided to write sentences using the comma correctly. ● In groups, learners are guided to engage in role play conversations in which the comma is used and then write down some sentences on a digital device. Why do you think we use a comma when writing?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. recognise the use of a comma correctly in a text,

   Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use the comma correctly in listing items,

   Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. adopt the use of the comma in writing. ● Individually, learner is guided to identify commas from writings on wall charts/ chalk board/digital and print resources. ● Individually, learner is guided to use the comma correctly in written exercises, with peers. ● In pairs, learners are guided to use commas to write lists of items/ names. ● In pairs, learners are guided to write sentences using the comma correctly. ● In groups, learners are guided to engage in role play conversations in which the comma is used and then write down some sentences on a digital device. Why do you think we use a comma when writing?

   Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: Teamwork as the learner engages in group practice exercises to write using a comma.

Digital literacy: Creating with technology is enhanced as the learner writes sentences with commas on digital devices.

Values:
Responsibility: Self-drive as learners takes up roles during role play activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: social cohesion as learners work together to identify commas in lists and sentence

Suggested Learning Resources

Adapted course book ,Chart, class readers, course books, flash cards, recording devices e.g tablets, mobile phone, laptop, dictionary, internet, audio- visual recordings

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. recognise the use of a comma correctly in a text,
2. use the comma correctly in listing items,
3. adopt the use of the comma in writing. ● Individually, learner is guided to identify commas from writings on wall charts/ chalk board/digital and print resources. ● Individually, learner is guided to use the comma correctly in written exercises, with peers. ● In pairs, learners are guided to use commas to write lists of items/ names. ● In pairs, learners are guided to write sentences using the comma correctly. ● In groups, learners are guided to engage in role play conversations in which the comma is used and then write down some sentences on a digital device.
